arxiv-2209-04979.title: Exploration of trace anomaly contribution to proton mass based on light vector meson photoproduction
arxiv-2209-04979.creator: Chen Dong, Jiyuan Zhang, Jingxuan Bu, Huifang Zhou, Xiao-Yun Wang
arxiv-2209-04979.description: Abstract In the quantum chromodynamics, the mass source of the proton is decomposed into four parts by the energy momentum tensor : quark energy term, gluon energy term, quark mass term and trace anomaly term. And the trace anomaly term is the most crucial contribution for studying the internal structure of the proton.

arxiv-2407-15685.description: Abstract . Today’s visualization tools for conveying the risks and benefits of AI technologies are largely tailored for those with technical expertise. To bridge this gap, we have developed a visualization that employs narrative patterns and interactive elements, enabling the broader public to gradually grasp the diverse risks and benefits associated with AI.

arxiv-2506-23349.description: Abstract Following the rise in popularity of data-centric machine learning (ML), various data valuation methods have been proposed to quantify the contribution of each datapoint to desired ML model performance metrics (e.g., accuracy). Beyond the technical applications of data valuation methods (e.g., data cleaning, data acquisition, etc.

arxiv-2508-01840.title: Implementing Neural Networks Over-the-Air via Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces
arxiv-2508-01840.creator: Meng Hua, Chenghong Bian, Haotian Wu, Deniz Gündüz
arxiv-2508-01840.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Meng Hua, Chenghong Bian, Haotian Wu, Deniz Gündüz. By leveraging the superposition property, over-the-air computation (OAC) of waveforms enables computations to be performed in an analog fashion in wireless environments, leading to faster computation, lower latency, and reduced energy consumption.

arxiv-2511-20102.description: Abstract The quadratic complexity of full attention limits efficient long-context processing in large language models (LLMs). Sparse attention mitigates this cost by restricting each query to attend to a subset of previous tokens; however, training-free approaches often lead to severe performance degradation. arxiv-2601-14242.title: APEX–Agents
arxiv-2601-14242.creator: Bertie Vidgen, Austin Mann, Abby Fennelly, John Wright Stanly, Marco Burstein, Julien Benchek, David Ostrofsky, Debnil Sur, Neel Venugopal, Alannah Hsia, Calix Huang, Olivia Varones, Daniyal Khan, Michael Haines, Chirag Mahapatra, Brendan Foody, Osvald Nitski, apex@mercor.com
arxiv-2601-14242.description: Abstract We introduce the AI Productivity Index for Agents ( APEX–Agents ), a benchmark for assessing whether AI agents can execute long-horizon, cross-application tasks created by investment banking analysts, management consultants, and corporate lawyers. APEX–Agents requires agents to navigate realistic work environments with files and tools. We test eight agents for the leaderboard using Pass@1.

arxiv-2602-11945.title: Towards Performance-Enhanced Model-Contrastive Federated Learning using Historical Information in Heterogeneous Scenarios
arxiv-2602-11945.creator: Hongliang Zhang, Jiguo Yu, Guijuan Wang, Wenshuo Ma, Tianqing He, Baobao Chai, Chunqiang Hu
arxiv-2602-11945.description: Abstract Federated Learning (FL) enables multiple nodes to collaboratively train a model without sharing raw data. However, FL systems are usually deployed in heterogeneous scenarios, where nodes differ in both data distributions and participation frequencies, which undermines the FL performance. To tackle the above issue, this paper proposes PMFL, a performance-enhanced model-contrastive federated learning framework using historical training information.

pmc-10701783.title: The phenomenon of spontaneous tumor regression in breast cancer
pmc-10701783.creator: Abid Qureshi, Sindhuri Gollamudi, Shahar Qureshi, Nisha Sondhi, Shahzaib Nabi, Romulo Genato, Philip Xiao, Armand Asarian
pmc-10701783.description: Spontaneous tumor regression is an increasingly prevalent phenomenon of partial or complete disappearance of primary tumor tissue or associated metastases in the absence of therapeutic intervention. Cases of spontaneous regression have been established in malignant tumors, such as testicular germ cell tumor, renal cell cancer, melanoma, basal cell carcinoma, neuroblastoma, colon cancer, breast cancer, as well as metastases.

pmc-10709314.title: The effect of uneven surfaces on inter-joint coordination during walking in children with cerebral palsy
pmc-10709314.creator: C Dussault-Picard, Y Cherni, A Ferron, M T Robert, P C Dixon
pmc-10709314.description: Clinical gait analysis on uneven surfaces contributes to the ecological assessment of gait deviations of children with spastic cerebral palsy (CP). Walking on uneven surfaces requires specific motor strategies, which can be assessed by lower-limb kinematic and inter-joint coordination analyses.

pmc-10743198.title: Molecular Characterization and Establishment of a Prognostic Model Based on Primary Immunodeficiency Features in Association with RNA Modifications in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer
pmc-10743198.creator: Hongzhuo Xia, Xi Xu, Yuxuan Guo, Xiyun Deng, Yian Wang, Shujun Fu, Kunqi Chen, Bowen Song, Fuyi Li
pmc-10743198.description: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is the most aggressive subtype of breast cancer. Although immunotherapy is effective for some patients, most find it difficult to benefit from it. This study aims to explore the impact of specific immune pathways and their regulated molecular mechanisms in TNBC.

pmc-11472730.title: Handgrip Evaluation Before and After Pulmonary Rehabilitation Therapy in Patients With Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD)
pmc-11472730.creator: Nestor A Diaz Posada, Diana J Cano Rosales, Maria C Amaya Muñoz, Mario A Buitrago Gomez, Silvia J Villabona, Paul Anthony Camacho López
pmc-11472730.description: IntroductionChronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) is a systemic disease characterized by skeletal muscle dysfunction, leading to increased morbidity and mortality and deteriorating quality of life. Pulmonary rehabilitation therapy improves symptoms and long-term adherence. This study aimed to evaluate how COPD patients respond to pulmonary rehabilitation therapy and its correlation with handgrip strength measurements.

pmc-11633810.title: A novel multi‐channel applicator with a U‐shaped channel for vaginal intracavity brachytherapy
pmc-11633810.creator: Yanfei Lu, Jianhong Chen, Fangfang Wang, Qiong Zhou, Xiang Zhang
pmc-11633810.description: BackgroundEndometrial cancer is one of the most common gynecological malignancies in the world. Vaginal brachytherapy is an important postoperative adjuvant treatment for endometrial cancer. However, a common problem with existing applicators is insufficient dose at the vaginal apex.PurposeThis study describes the Hangzhou (HZ) cylinder, a novel 3D printed vaginal intracavity brachytherapy applicator, detailing its characteristics, dose distribution, and clinical applications.

pmc-11647260.title: Exploring the therapeutic potential of diterpenes in gastric cancer: Mechanisms, efficacy, and clinical prospects
pmc-11647260.creator: Chenhui Ma, Lei Gao, Kewei Song, Baohong Gu, Bofang Wang, Weigao Pu, Hao Chen
pmc-11647260.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Gastric cancer (GC) remains a significant global health challenge, particularly prevalent in East Asia. Despite advancements in various treatment modalities, the prognosis for patients, especially those in advanced stages, remains poor, highlighting the need for innovative therapeutic approaches. This review explores the promising potential of diterpenes, naturally occurring compounds with robust anticancer properties, derived from diverse sources, such as plants, marine organisms, and fungi.

pmc-12385503.title: An Explainable Approach to Parkinson’s Diagnosis Using the Contrastive Explanation Method—CEM
pmc-12385503.creator: Ipek Balikci Cicek, Zeynep Kucukakcali, Birgul Deniz, Fatma Ebru Algül
pmc-12385503.description: Background/Objectives: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder that requires early and accurate diagnosis. This study aimed to classify individuals with and without PD using volumetric brain MRI data and to improve model interpretability using explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) techniques.

pmc-12425478.title: Structural evolution of nitrogenase over 3 billion years
pmc-12425478.creator: Bruno Cuevas Zuviría, Franka Detemple, Kaustubh Amritkar, Amanda K Garcia, Lance Seefeldt, Oliver Einsle, Betül Kaçar, Volker Dötsch, Bruno Cuevas Zuviría, Franka Detemple, Kaustubh Amritkar, Amanda K Garcia, Lance Seefeldt, Oliver Einsle, Betül Kaçar
pmc-12425478.description: Previously, we identified the only dinitrogen reduction mechanism known to date as an ancient feature conserved from nitrogenase ancestors, which we directly tested by resurrecting and integrating synthetic ancestral nitrogenases into the genome of Azotobacter vinelandii (Garcia et al., 2023), a genetically tractable, nitrogen-fixing model bacterium.

pmc-12472984.title: Therapeutic Potential of Probiotic-Derived P8 Protein as an Anti-Metastatic Agent in Colorectal Cancer
pmc-12472984.creator: Byung Chull An, Seungwoo Kim, Jaewon Ha, Sang-Hyuk Seok, Jun Won Park, Yongku Ryu, Myung Jun Chung, Alessandra Pino, Mutamed Ayyash
pmc-12472984.description: We previously described the use of probiotics to deliver a Lactobacillus rhamnosus-derived therapeutic protein, P8, which has been identified as a candidate colorectal cancer (CRC) suppressor protein with anti-proliferation and anti-migration activities. P8 was found to penetrate cell membranes by endocytosis, suppressing cell proliferation through G2 cell cycle arrest.

pmc-12606282.title: Integrative meta-analysis and experimental validation reveal the oncogenic role of SACS and its therapeutic targeting potential in colorectal cancer
pmc-12606282.creator: Chunmei Chen, Jun Li, Beibei Wen, Wenwei Dou, Haisheng Zhu
pmc-12606282.description: This study aims to identify core genes closely associated with the diagnosis and prognosis of colorectal cancer (CRC) using transcriptome-based meta-analysis approach and machine learning algorithms. Nine CRC datasets from the GEO database were integrated for differential gene expression analysis and WGCNA to identify key genes.

pmc-12874388.title: Comparing Force Field Treatments in QM/MM Studies of the SARS-CoV‑2 RNA-Dependent RNA Polymerase (RdRp) Mechanism
pmc-12874388.creator: Maite Roca, Yazdan Maghsoud, G. Andrés Cisneros, Katarzyna Świderek, Vicent Moliner
pmc-12874388.description: Molecular simulations have been instrumental in elucidating the SARS-CoV-2 lifecycle, thereby supporting the design and development of antiviral therapies and diagnostic tools for COVID-19. Here, the molecular mechanism of the SARS-CoV-2 RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp), a potential target for antiviral drugs to treat COVID-19, was explored based on QM/MM simulations with fixed-charge and polarizable force fields (cFF and pFF, respectively).

pmc-12966205.title: Reduced dose versus standard melphalan conditioning for autologous stem cell transplantation in multiple myeloma: a single-center retrospective study
pmc-12966205.creator: Yifan Yao, Shan Zhang, Ziying Li, Lili Luo, Xuan Lu, Huafang Wang
pmc-12966205.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This retrospective, single‑center study evaluated the efficacy and safety of a reduced‑dose melphalan conditioning regimen (140–180 mg/m2) for autologous stem cell transplantation (ASCT) in patients with multiple myeloma (MM) ineligible for the standard dose (200 mg/m2). Clinical outcomes were compared between patients receiving reduced‑dose versus standard‑dose melphalan over a five-year period, with pre‑specified subgroup analyses based on age and renal function.

pmc-13062089.title: AI based ECG data recovery and cardiovascular diseases classification (CEDRC-network)
pmc-13062089.creator: Muhammad Raheel Khan, Zunaib Maqsood Haider, Jawad Hussain, Masood Ahmad Khan, Saad Abdullah
pmc-13062089.description: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) are a significant and widespread cause of death in the world, continuing to increase mortality rates. Therefore, timely identification and diagnosis are essential for a patient’s optimized recovery and longevity. In this regard, ECG is an effective tool for detecting anomalous heart conditions.

pmc-13311327.title: NO modulates human airway smooth muscle function by altering glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase effects on sGC function in asthma
pmc-13311327.creator: Arnab Ghosh, Mamta P. Sumi, Cynthia Koziol-White, Blair Tupta, Ling Wang, Chaitali Ghosh, William F. Jester, Reynold A. Panettieri, Dennis J. Stuehr

pmc-13369782.title: Low-level Blood Multiple Metals Exposure from Informal Jewelry Welding Alters Metabolomic and Lipidomic Profiles in Brazilian Women
pmc-13369782.creator: Alda Neis Miranda de Araújo, Vinicius Guimarães Ferreira, Isabelle Nogueira Leroux, Danilo Cardoso de Oliveira, Andreia M Porcari, Kelly Polido Kaneshiro Olympio, Nilson Antônio de Assunção
pmc-13369782.description: Occupational exposure to toxic and potentially toxic elements (PTEs) remains a significant public health concern due to its potential to disrupt human metabolic processes. This study investigated metabolic and lipidomic alterations associated with blood PTE levels in Brazilian women engaged in informal, home-based jewelry welding.

pmc-13370069.title: SATB1 preserves CD4+ T-cell fidelity and establishes Treg function in antitumor immunity
pmc-13370069.creator: Wooseok Seo, Chengcheng Zou, Kanako Shimizu, Ruka Setoguchi, Kiyokazu Kakugawa, Terumi Kohwi-Shigematsu, Shohei Hori, Shin-ichiro Fujii, Hiroyoshi Nishikawa, Ichiro Taniuchi
pmc-13370069.description: SATB1 preserves CD4+ T-cell lineage fidelity by repressing Foxp3 in conventional T cells and is essential for establishing FoxP3-mediated gene repression in regulatory T cells. Deleting SATB1 disrupts Treg suppressive function, unleashing potent antitumor immunity. Introduction Special AT-rich sequence binding protein 1 (SATB1) is a crucial genome organizer that regulates T lymphocyte development and function (1, 2, 3).

pmc-13550339.title: Development and preclinical evaluation of selective vinyl sulfone-based probes for PET imaging of tumor-associated cathepsins
pmc-13550339.creator: Oliviero Cini, Alan Miranda, Daan Willocx, Angeliki Karakasidi, Anke de Groot, Thales do Valle Moreira, Ana P. Leandro, Maria M. M. Santos, Rui Moreira, Filipe Elvas
pmc-13550339.description: BackgroundCysteine cathepsin L (CatL) is emerging as a key biomarker of cancer progression, making it an attractive candidate for non-invasive molecular imaging. To monitor enzymatic activity directly, rather than merely protein expression, activity-based probes (ABPs) enable selective targeting of enzymes through covalent binding at their active sites.
